title: Blanquette de Veau
subtitle: Classic French white veal stew in a cream sauce
excerpt: One of the great French braises: pale veal shoulder simmered gently in an aromatic white stock, the cooking liquid finished with egg yolks and cream to a rich, velvety sauce. Served with rice and a scattering of parsley.

recipe.sourceNotes: Blanquette de veau is one of the canonical French braises, classified as a white stew (a ragout blanc) because neither the meat nor the sauce is browned. This keeps the dish pale, delicate, and unlike almost any other meat preparation in French cooking. The dish appears in Escoffier's Le Guide Culinaire and in virtually every French culinary text of the twentieth century as an exemplar of the French technique of finishing sauces with a liaison of egg yolks and cream, which thickens without boiling. Veal's mild, delicate flavour makes it the ideal vehicle for this treatment: a more strongly flavoured meat would overwhelm the subtlety of the sauce. Traditionally the dish also contains pearl onions and button mushrooms cooked separately and added at the end.

recipeTools.notes: A large, wide saucepan or casserole.

content.text: The crucial step is the liaison: whisk the egg yolks and cream together in a bowl, then ladle some of the hot broth into this mixture to temper it before adding it back to the pan. Never add cold cream and eggs directly to boiling liquid or they will scramble. Once the liaison is added, do not boil the sauce: heat it gently until it thickens slightly and coats the back of a spoon.

Blanch the veal: place the pieces in a large saucepan, cover with cold water, bring to the boil, and drain immediately. Rinse the meat under cold water. Return the meat to the pan and cover with 1.5 litres of fresh cold water. Add the onion, carrot, celery, leek, garlic, thyme, bay leaves, and cloves. Bring to a simmer and cook gently for 1 to 1.25 hours until the veal is very tender.

Remove the veal and strain the broth; you need about 800 ml. Make a velouté: melt the butter in the saucepan, stir in the flour, and cook for 1 minute. Gradually whisk in the warm broth and cook over medium heat for 10 minutes until smooth and thickened.

Whisk the egg yolks and cream together in a bowl. Ladle about 200 ml of the hot sauce into the cream mixture, whisking constantly. Pour this liaison back into the sauce. Heat over low heat, stirring, until the sauce coats the back of a spoon; do not boil. Add the lemon juice and season with salt. Return the veal and mushrooms to the sauce. Serve with rice or egg noodles, scattered with parsley.
